webhook_secret: <ask your admin — sent as the X-Enrichment-Secret header, never a real value in this file>
n8n_api_key: <ask your admin — n8n Settings > n8n API; sent as the X-N8N-API-KEY header on read-only status calls, a DIFFERENT secret from webhook_secret, never a real value in this file>
_n8n_monthly_execution_allowance_note: Must equal config/execution_budget.yaml's monthly_execution_allowance in the backend repo — tests/test_execution_budget_drift.py fails when the two disagree. Powers the burn-rate alarm (Phase 45 ALARM-03): a missing, blank or non-positive value here means the sweep is NOT watching the execution budget at all.
_n8n_schedule_floor_max_share_note: Must equal config/execution_budget.yaml's idle_floor_max_share in the backend repo. Consumed by the runtime cadence budget floor (Phase 45); present here because this file is the plugin's one config surface.
_burn_rate_alarm_threshold_note: The burn-rate alarm fires when the sampled execution rate, projected over 30 days, exceeds n8n_monthly_execution_allowance times this value. 1.0 is the default ceiling — the idle floor is roughly 4% of a 2,500/month plan, so any real anomaly clears it by an order of magnitude.
hubspot_portal_id: <optional — your HubSpot portal id, used only to build a clickable record link in the review queue; without it the queue shows the raw record id>
_enrichment_providers_note: THIS DEFAULT ENABLES EVERY PROVIDER ON EVERY ENRICHMENT BATCH. Three valid settings: the full waterfall (the list above), a named subset (e.g. ["lusha"]), or none ([]). You can override any of the three for a single batch — say the override when you ask for the batch, and the preview states the selection that batch will actually use before you approve it.
_enrichment_providers_cost_note: Rough provider-credit burn per record on a first-time enrich, measured 2026-07-30: Lusha 1 credit per contact and 2 credits per company (0 credits when re-enriching a stored Lusha id); ZoomInfo about 1.08 credits per match; Apollo unknown — this account's key is not a master key, so its balance reads 403 and is reported as unknown, never as zero. Anthropic model spend measured at about $0.0686 per record (Phase 22 canary, 2026-07-30). Set this to [] to run a batch that burns no provider credits at all.
_max_records_per_chunk_note: CONFIRMED 2026-08-03 by live probe B4: one full-waterfall record (lusha+apollo+zoominfo) took 37.44 s. Worst case observed 37.44 s, plus 25% headroom = 46.8 s per record, against the roughly 100 s Cloudflare response ceiling on an n8n Cloud webhook. floor(100 / 46.8) = 2. The enrichment workflow has no batching node, so every record in one POST runs the full provider + Haiku + Sonnet chain before the response fires.
_max_records_per_chunk_provenance_note: B4 — the expensive path this ceiling had to survive — ran live 2026-08-03 and confirmed 2. The multi-record no-provider probes (B2/B3) remain unrun; they can only lower per-record time, not raise it, so they cannot move the ceiling down further and are not required. Note: the live oversize-refusal check could not be exercised the same day — the deployed enrichment workflow predates the committed list lane and answered object_type=unsupported; re-run it after the next disarmed deploy.
_max_rows_per_match_request_note: Equals the backend's ENRICH_MAX_PROPOSE_RECORDS (scripts/build_cloud_workflows.py) BY CONSTRUCTION — this value is read out of that constant, never computed from an independent client-side formula, so the two cannot drift into disagreeing about the same bound. A match POST runs zero provider calls (two HubSpot searches only, no Haiku/Sonnet chain), which is why this ceiling differs from max_records_per_chunk's write-path bound above. To raise it: raise ENRICH_MAX_PROPOSE_RECORDS first, then this key second — backend first, always, because a client that chunks above the backend's bound produces a refusal for a batch the preview already approved.
_max_rows_per_match_request_provenance_n: MEASURED 2026-08-05, live 9-row walk (37-09's operator checkpoint): 13.16 s / 9 rows = 1.46 s/row, so 20 rows at that rate is ~29 s against the ~100 s Cloudflare-enforced ceiling — well inside it. 20 was originally the backend's own conservative propose-mode ASSUMPTION (worst case 4 s/row, +25% headroom, floor(100/5)=20); the value is unchanged by this measurement (raising it is a separate deliberate decision, not a consequence of measuring), but this bound is now backed by an actual live measurement, not an assumption — no longer a placeholder awaiting one. Mirrored in scripts/build_cloud_workflows.py's ENRICH_MAX_PROPOSE_RECORDS comment.
_watch_bound_seconds_note: MEASURED 2026-07-31 (29-TIMING.md), n=5 enrichment executions: 32.1-38.9 s wall clock, 35.6-36.1 s/record on the 2 that carried a recoverable record count. 600 s (10 min) is ~15x the observed max single-run duration, chosen with headroom because a bound set too LOW trains the operator to stop believing a 'still running' message at all (NOTICE-02) — a bound set too high only costs a slightly later message. Scales as max(600, records * 45) for a multi-record dispatch (the enrichment workflow has no batching node, so an N-record dispatch takes roughly N times as long). Raise this if your backend is consistently slower than that; no code change needed.
